messages.subject: N-Mixture models using pcountopen function
parts:
Dear all,

I'm new in unmarked and I'm trying to calculate the abundance of several bird species in urban enviroments by the use of N-Mixture models. I was counting birds in 60 points for 2 years following the Pollock's robust model: 12 counts in two years, 3 per each season (winter and summer of each year). 

Now I want to model the abundance of some species but incorporating the detectability of these species. After reading several papers and information provided in this group, I decided to use a single especies - multi-season approach by the use of the function pcountopen. However I'm only interested in model the abundance and detectability of these species and the effect on them of some covariables, not probabilities of colonization or extinction.

My first question: Is this the right approach and function in umarked? the 

Second: I have been using a model selection approach: is neccesary let  gamma (ext) and epsilon (col) as constants? or should be also included variables to model this aspects?   

Third: what are the differences between outputs of predict() and ranef() for pcount models? if I want to obtain an estimated of the final modeled abundance by specie can I use an average of the ranef or predict values (and ICs) of the two years? 

Kind regards

Juan Amaya
